prompt: Why does the debug build type get `applicationIdSuffix = ".debug"`?
hint: Look at the two package names `aapt2` printed.

choices.text: So it installs beside the release, as a separate app
choices.why: Right: two package names, two apps, two sets of data.

choices.text: So that R8 skips it
choices.why: R8 is off in debug because `isMinifyEnabled` is only set in release.

choices.text: Because Google Play refuses a package name without a suffix
choices.why: The release has no suffix and is the one Play receives.

choices.text: To mark it as debuggable
choices.why: The build type itself makes it debuggable; the suffix only changes the id.

prompt: Which of these belongs in a build type rather than in the app's code?
hint: A build type changes how, never what.

choices.text: A setting the student picks in the app
choices.why: A choice made at run time cannot live in the build.

choices.text: A feature that only debug builds show
choices.why: Then the build that ships was never tested with it.

choices.text: Turning R8 on
choices.why: Right: it changes how the app is built, not what it does.

choices.text: A different home screen for testers on the release build
choices.why: That changes what the app does.

prompt: How many APKs did `assembleDebug` build in section 02, once the two flavours existed?
What is the planner's `direct` flavour for?

choices.text: A build that talks straight to the database
choices.why: Both flavours share every line of code.

choices.text: Phones with no Play Store
choices.why: Right: handed out as a file from the planner's website.

choices.text: A version for testers only
choices.why: Testers are reached through Play's testing tracks, section 08.

choices.text: Running the app straight from Android Studio without installing it
choices.why: Every variant is installed to run.

prompt: A project has two flavour dimensions of three flavours each, and the two build types. How many variants does it have?
The planner wants a premium tier with extra statistics. Why is a `premium` flavour the wrong tool?

choices.text: `BuildConfig` cannot hold a boolean
choices.why: It can; that is not the problem.

choices.text: Flavours cannot change code, only resources
choices.why: A `src/premium/` folder could carry code; the objection is elsewhere.

choices.text: The student chooses it, and a flavour is fixed when the app is built
choices.why: Right: two installs, two sets of data and two listings for one person.

choices.text: Google Play allows only one flavour per account
choices.why: Play sees applications, not flavours.

prompt: Why is the password read with `read -rs` and not typed into the `keytool` command?
hint: Where does a typed command go afterwards?

choices.text: Gradle can only read a variable that `read` created
choices.why: Any exported variable works; `read` just avoids typing it in a command.

choices.text: It makes the password longer
choices.why: Length is whatever you type.

choices.text: `keytool` refuses a password on the command line
choices.why: It accepts one; that is the risk.

choices.text: The shell's history would keep it
choices.why: Right, and `-s` keeps it off the screen too.

prompt: A release build fails at `:app:validateSigningPlayRelease` with `Keystore file not set for signing config upload`, and the file is in `~/keys`. What do you check first?
hint: The message names the wrong culprit.

choices.text: Whether `PLANNER_UPLOAD_PASSWORD` is set in this terminal
choices.why: Right: section 04's failure was exactly that.

choices.text: Whether the keystore was created with `-keyalg RSA`
choices.why: The algorithm does not make the configuration incomplete.

choices.text: Whether `isMinifyEnabled` is true
choices.why: R8 runs after validation; this failed before it.

choices.text: Whether the key has expired
choices.why: It is valid until 2051.

prompt: Why did section 04 make the key valid for 9,125 days?
hint: What happens to updates when a key expires?

choices.text: That is the longest validity `keytool` allows
choices.why: `keytool` accepts longer; 25 years is Google's recommendation.

choices.text: Google Play rejects keys valid for less than that
choices.why: It is a recommendation, as section 04 quoted it.

choices.text: Google recommends 25 years, because an app signed by an expired key cannot be updated
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A 4,096-bit RSA key needs it
choices.why: Key size and validity are independent.

prompt: In section 05, how did the `play` APK's size change between debug and release?

choices.text: It grew, because release adds a signature
choices.why: Both are signed; the release is far smaller.

choices.text: About the same, because R8 only renames
choices.why: It removes as well as renames.

choices.text: From 11.7 MB to 0.76 MB
choices.why: Right: most of it was library code the planner never calls.

choices.text: From 27.82 MB to 11.7 MB
choices.why: 27.82 MB was lesson 1's uncompressed dex, not an APK.

prompt: Why did `com.example.planner.MainActivity` keep its name when `ComponentActivity` became `k9`?
hint: Who refers to it by a string?

choices.text: `proguard-rules.pro` has a `-keep` line for it
choices.why: The planner's rules file keeps nothing.

choices.text: Compose classes are excluded from obfuscation
choices.why: `AndroidComposeView` became `h2`.

choices.text: The manifest names it
choices.why: Right: R8 keeps what the manifest refers to.

choices.text: R8 never renames the app's own classes, only libraries'
choices.why: It renames any class nothing names by string.

prompt: A release build crashes and the stack trace names `h2`. What do you need to read it?
hint: A file written by every release build.

choices.text: Any `mapping.txt` from the same version name
choices.why: Two builds of one version can map names differently.

choices.text: The `mapping.txt` of the exact build that crashed
choices.why: Right, which is why it is kept with each release.

choices.text: A `-keep` rule added after the crash
choices.why: That changes the next build, not this trace.

choices.text: The debug build's stack trace for the same crash
choices.why: The debug build may not crash at all; R8 is what differs.

prompt: What does Google Play require new apps to upload?

choices.text: A universal APK
choices.why: An APK is what a phone installs; Play wants the input it builds them from.

choices.text: One APK per processor family
choices.why: Play builds those itself, from the bundle.

choices.text: The source code and `mapping.txt`
choices.why: Play never receives source code.

choices.text: An Android App Bundle
choices.why: Right: a `.aab`.

prompt: Why did the bundle's `base/lib/` hold the same library four times?

choices.text: A backup in case one copy is damaged
choices.why: The four folders are four processors.

choices.text: One build per processor family, and each phone gets one
choices.why: Right: Play's split APKs carry only the one a phone needs.

choices.text: One per flavour and build type
choices.why: The bundle is one variant, `playRelease`.

choices.text: R8 duplicates native code to optimise it
choices.why: R8 works on dex, not on native libraries.

prompt: Which file in the bundle carries the upload key's signature?

choices.text: `META-INF/UPLOAD.RSA`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `base/manifest/AndroidManifest.xml`
choices.why: The manifest names the app's parts, not who signed it.

choices.text: `BundleConfig.pb`
choices.why: That describes how Play may split the bundle.

choices.text: `base/resources.pb`
choices.why: That is the resources, in a format Play reads.

prompt: With Play App Signing, which key signs the APKs that phones install?

choices.text: The debug key
choices.why: That never leaves your computer's debug builds.

choices.text: The app signing key, which Google keeps
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Each phone's own key
choices.why: A phone checks a signature; it does not sign apps.

choices.text: Your upload key
choices.why: That signs what you upload, and Play checks it.

prompt: You lose the upload key of an app on Google Play with Play App Signing. What then?

choices.text: The app must be republished under a new package name
choices.why: That is the fate of the `direct` flavour, not of this one.

choices.text: You request an upload key reset
choices.why: Right: updates keep installing, because the app signing key is unchanged.

choices.text: Phones uninstall the app at the next update
choices.why: Phones only see the app signing key, which is unchanged.

choices.text: Nothing: the upload key is not checked
choices.why: Play checks it on every upload.

prompt: Students installed the `direct` APK from the website. Its key is lost. What can reach their phones now?
hint: Every update is checked against the installed key.

choices.text: The same APK, re-signed with the debug key
choices.why: A different key is a different key, debug or not.

choices.text: An update signed with a new key, after a warning
choices.why: The phone refuses it outright; there is no warning to accept.

choices.text: An update after a reset requested from Google
choices.why: Google never held this key, so there is nothing to reset.

choices.text: No update: only a new app under a new name
choices.why: Right: for that flavour the key is the app.

prompt: From 31 August 2026, what must a new app or update target to be submitted to Google Play?

choices.text: API 36 or higher
choices.why: Right: Android 16.

choices.text: API 37, the `compileSdk`
choices.why: `compileSdk` is what the app compiles against; the rule is about `targetSdk`.

choices.text: API 34 or higher
choices.why: Below the requirement section 08 quoted.

choices.text: API 35 or higher
choices.why: That is the floor for existing apps to stay visible to new users.

prompt: You upload a second bundle with the same `versionCode` as the first. What happens?

choices.text: It replaces the first one on every phone
choices.why: It never gets that far.

choices.text: Play increments the code for you
choices.why: The code is yours to set, in the build file.

choices.text: Play accepts it if `versionName` differs
choices.why: `versionName` is for people; Play compares the code.

choices.text: The console refuses it
choices.why: Right: `versionCode` must grow with every upload.

prompt: Put the steps from bundle to store in the order section 08 gives them.
hint: Signing comes before the first upload.
items: create the app in the Play Console
upload the bundle to a testing track
fill in the store listing and the declarations

prompt: Which of these is a sign that the planner should be split into modules?

choices.text: The app uses Room
choices.why: A library is not a reason to split.

choices.text: The release build takes over a minute
choices.why: That is R8 reading everything, which a split does not avoid.

choices.text: The app has more than one screen
choices.why: The planner has had several since early lessons, in one module.

choices.text: A screen imports a DAO and nothing stops it
choices.why: Right: a module boundary makes that not compile.

right_distractors: chooses the flavour at run time

prompt: To make a variant install beside another on one phone, the build file sets `___` on it.
A release build works on your phone and crashes on a tester's, while the debug build works on both. Which suspect does this lesson point to first?
hint: What differs between debug and release?

choices.text: The tester's phone has the debug build installed
choices.why: With the suffix the two live side by side.

choices.text: A class reached by reflection that R8 removed or renamed
choices.why: Right: a missing `-keep` rule shows up only in release.

choices.text: The upload key expired
choices.why: An expired key stops updates; it does not crash a running app.

choices.text: The `direct` flavour
choices.why: Both builds here are the same flavour.
